clue.text: Was first to see a pattern that threatens the monarch

definitions.note: a describing clause for a noun phrase: the thing that threatens the king

blocks.note: to discover something is to be the first to see it
a check is a pattern of squares, as on a tablecloth

explanation.surface: Someone spots a sinister design aimed at the king before anyone else does.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess, the monarch is the king; a DISCOVERED CHECK happens when one piece moves out of the way and uncovers an attack on the king by another.
explanation.definitionFit: This chess term names an attack on the king revealed by moving a different piece out of the line.

clue.text: Arranging to take power, but refusing to take advantage

indicators.note: taking something means holding it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: sorting things is arranging them
P is the standard abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A schemer plots to seize power yet declines to exploit the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: SORTING takes P after its first letter, giving SPORTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting person plays fair and will not exploit an opponent's misfortune, like a good sport.

clue.text: Frustrate one buttoned up for Olympic event

definitions.text: one buttoned up for Olympic event

blocks.note: first meaning: to thwart or block a plan

blocks.clueFragment: one buttoned up for Olympic event
blocks.note: second meaning: the light fencing sword whose tip is covered by a small button for safety

explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttoned up' suggests a fastened coat, but it means a blade with a button on its point; fencing is an Olympic sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To foil a scheme is to thwart it, and a foil is also a blunted fencing weapon with a safety tip.

clue.text: Not forced to disband one platoon

indicators.note: a disbanded unit scatters and breaks up, so the letters are dispersed and regrouped

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers are told breaking up a unit is voluntary rather than compulsory.
explanation.walkthrough: The military surface makes 'Not forced' read like troops, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is left to choice, not required or compelled by anyone.

clue.text: Be after contract United accepted

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so one piece is received inside the other

blocks.note: to purse the lips is to contract or pucker them
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football club chases a deal that it has agreed to sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun for a deal but is the verb, as in pursing the lips; PURSE takes U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue something is to chase it or seek it, so being after it is a synonym phrase.

clue.text: State that is briefly satisfactory

blocks.note: surface reading: a condition that is fine for a short while
setter's reading: a US state whose postal abbreviation is the two-letter word for 'all right'

explanation.walkthrough: 'State' reads as a condition and 'briefly' as 'for a short time'; really 'briefly' means abbreviated, and this state's code is OK.
explanation.definitionFit: The American state's two-letter postal code is OK, which is also a common word for acceptable.

clue.text: Cut of meat, second to go bad

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
eggs that addle go rotten

explanation.surface: A butcher's joint has only a moment before it spoils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' simply places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle of lamb or venison is a joint taken from both loins of the animal's back.

clue.text: Be very discreet and retain a personal lawyer

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for keeping your thoughts and plans to yourself
second meaning, read literally: to keep (retain) a barrister (counsel) of your own

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read word by word: keep = retain, one's = personal, counsel = a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means saying nothing of your intentions, staying silent and secretive about private matters.

clue.text: I am at concert, and put out a piece of music

indicators.note: something knocked out of place is disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: contracted to I'm
a prom is a promenade concert, as at the London Proms
taken as written

explanation.surface: A concertgoer claims to have been flustered by a musical item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as annoyed, but 'out' is the signal working on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu is a short free-form composition, often for solo piano, as by Schubert or Chopin.

clue.text: One rascal that can beat nine or ten

definitions.text: that can beat nine or ten
definitions.note: a describing clause standing for the playing card

blocks.note: first meaning: a dishonest rogue

blocks.clueFragment: that can beat nine or ten
blocks.note: second meaning: the court card ranking just above the ten in a suit

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a brawler beating up several people; really it is a card outranking the nine and ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is an old word for a scoundrel and also the jack in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Composer’s heart problem returned

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the core is the heart or centre of something
an ill is a trouble or misfortune

explanation.surface: A composer's cardiac trouble has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart problem' looks like one medical phrase, but splits into two pieces; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist and composer of concerti grossi.

clue.text: Fail to appear for pub performance perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: to miss a date without warning
second meaning: solo comedy routines, often staged in pubs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a no-show at a gig; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone up is to jilt them at a meeting, and a stand-up act is live comedy.

clue.text: Unoccupied, love to be cast in a film

indicators.note: an actor cast in a movie is placed within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: vid is short for video, a film
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: An out-of-work actor would love a part in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unoccupied' sounds like an idle actor, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A void place is empty, with nothing and nobody in it, as in an empty seat.

clue.text: Queen bee only confused by a new name

indicators.note: confused things are muddled out of order, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A queen bee alone is baffled by a new label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen bee' looks like one insect, but 'Queen' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn was the second wife of Henry VIII and Queen of England, executed in 1536.

clue.text: Create lines on paper for soft toy

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
to do something can mean to make or produce it
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A child draws lines on a sheet of paper to design a cuddly toy.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the first part after the second, so the paper comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag doll is a cuddly toy made from stuffed cloth, an example of a soft plaything.

clue.text: Say, Roman soldier up in old tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a GI is an American soldier
the larch is a conifer

explanation.surface: A legionary climbs into an ancient tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman soldier' looks like a legionary, but 'Say, Roman' is the definition: Roman Abramovich, the Russian billionaire who owned Chelsea football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman Abramovich is a famous example of a Russian tycoon wielding wealth and influence.

clue.text: Runs on the shore, having to live with twinges

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
twinges are small pains

explanation.surface: A jogger trots along the sand, putting up with sore muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' suggests jogging, but it means drives a boat aground.
explanation.definitionFit: To beach a vessel is to run it aground onto sand deliberately.

clue.text: Express disapproval of girl with glasses going to dance

blocks.note: to boo is to jeer
gal is a casual word for a girl
two O shapes look like a pair of spectacles

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at a bespectacled girl heading off to a disco.
explanation.walkthrough: OO for glasses is a crossword convention from the shape of spectacle lenses.
explanation.definitionFit: The boogaloo is a 1960s style of rhythm-and-blues dancing popular in America.

clue.text: March round in ragged sort of progression

indicators.note: something ragged is torn and untidy, so the letters are roughed up into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a round shape is the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops march in untidy formation, a sort of procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March round' looks like a parade instruction; 'progression' is the definition, used in maths and music.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonic progression is a mathematical sequence of reciprocals, and also a chord sequence in music.

clue.text: Old Chancellor not going about town

indicators.note: turning about means facing back the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Alistair Darling was UK Chancellor of the Exchequer from 2007 to 2010
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former finance minister declines to tour the town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister; 'not going about' reads as staying put but is the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlington is a market town in County Durham in north-east England, famous for early railways.

clue.text: Object to being given another errand?

definitions.note: read as RE-SENT, a past participle

blocks.note: first meaning: to feel bitter about something
second meaning, split as two parts: sent again on a mission

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split: someone sent out once more has been sent a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel aggrieved by it; re-sent describes being dispatched again.

clue.text: As authority, accepts passes

blocks.note: first meaning: follows a rule or source, as in following the book
second meaning: moves past, as time does

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an official approving a permit; the comma splits the clue into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by the rules means to follow them, and time or traffic that goes by moves past.

clue.text: Energy from writer, one moving along

indicators.note: a single letter, one, shifts its place in the word, so the order changes

blocks.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, from the brand name

explanation.surface: A writer gets energy from someone else passing by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is I, and the I in BIRO slides one place along to give BRIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or liveliness, especially in performance, a synonym for vitality and verve.

clue.text: Recoil from being pierced by a stone shaped like a spear point

indicators.note: a pierced thing has something pushed through it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: to hate something is to recoil from it
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: Someone flinches from being stabbed by a spear-tipped flint.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastate is a botanical term for leaves with a triangular, arrowhead-like base, from the Latin for spear.

clue.text: I won’t mention the rest, even quickly

blocks.note: 'and' can add emphasis like 'even', as in 'he refused, and rudely'
soon means before long, quickly

explanation.surface: A speaker skips the details, even rushing what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole sentence, the speaker's way of cutting a list short.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to wave away further items in a list without naming them, like et cetera.

clue.text: Dip into Brown Book at last

indicators.note: 'at last' points to the final position, so only the end letter is kept

blocks.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets round to reading a Brown novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown Book' suggests an author such as Dan Brown; they are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To dunk is to dip food briefly into liquid, like a biscuit in tea.

clue.text: Study one initially complicated section of maths

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
the Roman numeral for one
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A student studies a tricky part of the maths syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section' looks like part of a course, but a conic is itself a section, the curve made by slicing a cone.
explanation.definitionFit: A conic, short for conic section, is a curve such as an ellipse or parabola studied in geometry.

clue.text: Edible grains in near frozen state stuck to part of face

blocks.note: the brow is the forehead
NR is the abbreviation for near
ice is water in its frozen state

explanation.surface: Grains of food, almost frozen, get stuck to someone's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near frozen' reads as almost frozen, but splits into two pieces; 'stuck to' places them after the face part.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown rice is unpolished rice with the bran left on, a wholegrain cereal food.
